assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
The day analysed (18 Sep 2026) is compared with 17 Sep 2026, the immediately preceding period of equal length; the deeper checks compare 17-18 Sep with the 10-16 Sep baseline.

facts.text: Card success rate on 18 Sep was 76.75%, the lowest day in the 22-day window; the median daily rate was 86.72%.

Over 17-18 Sep, card attempt success rate fell 9.24pp from 87.0% to 77.75% versus 10-16 Sep (28,445 baseline attempts vs 7,956 current attempts). The change is statistically and practically significant.

Kestrel Bank is the segment that most concentrates the drop: its card success rate fell from 86.87% to 57.8%. The other acquirers moved little: Northstar Bank 86.65% to 85.2%, Meridian Bank 86.98% to 87.77%, Saffron Bank 87.5% to 87.17%, none of them significant.
Within Kestrel Bank, all three card methods fell sharply: debit card down 30.11pp (86.42% to 56.31%), credit card down 28.71pp (88.64% to 59.94%) and card EMI down 23.87pp (80.67% to 56.8%).
For Kestrel Bank, acquirer timeouts (ACQ_TIMEOUT) rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the current window vs 22 in the baseline). Other failure codes were flat or slightly lower.
Across all card payments, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.24 to 10.24 per 100 attempts (815 failures in the current window); no other code moved by more than 0.26 per 100 attempts.

The Kestrel Bank card problem ran from 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00 (36 hours). The worst hour was 18 Sep 02:00 at a 36.36% success rate, against a reference of 86.87%. About 716 excess failed attempts occurred out of 2,229 affected attempts.
Significant drops in success rate appeared across hours 8 and 10 to 23; the largest was at hour 12, down 13.64pp.
The data-quality scan found no issues.

response.headline: Card success rate on 18 Sep fell to 76.75%, the lowest day in the period against a typical 86.72%, and the drop is concentrated in Kestrel Bank, where card payments fell from 86.9% to 57.8%.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Kestrel Bank for their incident log for 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00, and check gateway-side connection and latency metrics for that route.
hypotheses.rationale: The decline is isolated to one acquirer across all card methods, the failures are almost entirely acquirer timeouts, the other acquirers are unaffected, and the issue has a clear start and end time.
hypotheses.text: A technical outage or degradation on the Kestrel Bank acquiring connection caused the drop, with requests timing out before getting a response.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A technical outage or degradation on the Kestrel Bank acquiring connection caused the drop
recommendations.rationale: The timeout spike and 36-hour window point to an acquirer-side or connectivity issue that needs the acquirer's confirmation.
recommendations.text: Raise an incident review with Kestrel Bank to confirm the root cause and get written confirmation that the timeouts are resolved.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The Kestrel Bank card problem ran from 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00 (36 hours).
recommendations.rationale: The problem lasted 36 hours and cost about 716 excess failed attempts; faster detection and rerouting would limit the impact.
recommendations.text: Set up an alert on ACQ_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts and on hourly success rate per acquirer, and review whether traffic can be failed over to other acquirers automatically during such events.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Kestrel Bank is the segment that most concentrates the drop
recommendations.rationale: The outage window ended 18 Sep 22:00, and sustained recovery should be verified.
recommendations.text: Re-check Kestrel Bank card success rate over the next few days to confirm recovery to roughly the 86.9% reference level.
